summary: Add fail-closed AI-agent governance with immutable per-agent tool policy, hard action/frequency limits, tenant/agent/integration kill switches, prompt-injection trust classification, bounded provenance and direct MCP enforcement before audit/tool execution.

impacts.evidence: Tenant scope and agent/integration identity are server-derived. Policies, kill switches, counters and usage receipts use composite organization/workspace keys, workspace foreign keys and forced RLS; tool/prompt input cannot select authority.

External/model text is classified untrusted rather than stored as authority. MCP source facts are marked UNTRUSTED_TOOL_DATA, counterparty agent output is minimized, and audit/provenance keeps bounded identifiers/digests rather than raw prompt/provider content.
The existing additive MCP developer surface gains stricter server-side governance and additive result provenance metadata. REST/OpenAPI operation paths and schemas are unchanged.
Task 079 adds no event type or event schema. Sensitive MCP price intent still enters the existing Task-017 governance approval event/outbox path.
Connector SDK v1, Runtime and provider manifests are unchanged. Governance is an application/platform boundary and provider implementations receive no agent policy authority.
Additive migration 000026 creates forced-RLS AI policy, kill-switch, call-counter and usage-receipt tables with immutable/version guards and no backfill; old readers/writers remain compatible.

Exact tool/permission/risk policy, hard write limits, fail-closed kill switches and prohibited secret/private-key capabilities are enforced after normal authorization and before MCP audit/tool execution. Policy/control-plane state is never model supplied.

Sensitive-write policies are invalid without approval_required and commerce.price.change.request remains Task-017 approval-only. Server-parsed price money must also satisfy the active agent limit before an approval request can be created.

MCP Task-003 audit and tool-result metadata now carry bounded agent/model/run/integration/correlation/policy/risk/context provenance. Immutable policy/kill/usage history preserves governance evidence without introducing raw prompt lineage.

Frequency enforcement persists one append-only decision receipt per tenant invocation id; exact retries return the original decision without double-consuming the window, while semantic invocation reuse conflicts. Existing Task-017 price-request idempotency remains unchanged.
Agent governance performs no arbitrary network/webhook egress and adds no connector credential access. Future egress tools must still pass canonical application/provider boundaries.

Policy id/version, risk, context-trust and kill-switch version are bounded decision dimensions, while durable call usage/counters provide rate evidence. Arbitrary prompt text is intentionally excluded from observability metadata.

Tenant/agent/integration kill switches provide immediate fail-closed operational stop. The schema is additive; application rollback retains immutable policy/kill/usage evidence rather than destructively removing security history.

Unit/integration-boundary tests cover policy/risk/limits, kill-switch failures, durable-repository migration invariants, MCP hiding/denial and an executable prompt-injection corpus including malicious external text, over-limit money and prohibited private-key access.
